questions.q: State the three factors that determine the amount of depreciation for a fixed asset under Accounting Standard-6.
questions.a: The three factors are: (1) Cost of the asset (historical cost including acquisition, installation, and commissioning), (2) Estimated net residual (salvage) value, and (3) Estimated useful life of the asset. A wrong answer (e.g., "market value, physical life, inflation") reveals the student is confusing depreciation accounting with valuation or physical deterioration concepts.

questions.q: A machine is purchased for ₹5,00,000. Freight and installation cost ₹50,000. The estimated scrap value after 10 years is ₹60,000, and disposal expenses are estimated at ₹10,000. What is the depreciable cost? Explain why the purchase price alone is not the depreciable cost.
questions.a: Depreciable cost = (₹5,00,000 + ₹50,000) – (₹60,000 – ₹10,000) = ₹5,50,000 – ₹50,000 = ₹5,00,000. Purchase price alone ignores incidental costs necessary to make the asset usable and ignores net residual value. A student who answers ₹5,00,000 (ignoring freight/installation) or ₹4,50,000 (ignoring disposal costs) misunderstands the definition of "cost" and "net residual value" per AS-6.

questions.q: A company buys a second-hand machine for ₹2,00,000, spends ₹25,000 on overhauling, and ₹5,000 on transportation. It estimates a useful life of 5 years and a net residual value of ₹30,000. Calculate the annual depreciation under the straight-line method. Show the steps.
questions.a: Step 1: Cost = ₹2,00,000 + ₹25,000 + ₹5,000 = ₹2,30,000. Step 2: Net residual value = ₹30,000. Step 3: Depreciable cost = ₹2,30,000 – ₹30,000 = ₹2,00,000. Step 4: Annual depreciation = ₹2,00,000 / 5 = ₹40,000. A wrong answer (e.g., ₹46,000 using only purchase price, or ₹40,000 but with wrong cost calculation) shows the student cannot correctly assemble the cost components or apply the formula.

questions.q: Compare two assets: Asset A (cost ₹10,00,000, residual ₹1,00,000, life 9 years) and Asset B (cost ₹10,00,000, residual ₹2,00,000, life 8 years). Which has a higher annual depreciation charge under straight-line? Justify without full calculation.
questions.a: Asset A: depreciable cost ₹9,00,000 / 9 = ₹1,00,000 per year. Asset B: depreciable cost ₹8,00,000 / 8 = ₹1,00,000 per year. They are equal. A student who picks one asset as higher without calculating reveals they treat factors in isolation rather than seeing the combined effect of (cost – residual) / life.

questions.q: Critique this statement: "If a machine's useful life is extended from 5 to 10 years due to better maintenance, the total depreciation charged over its life will double." Use the concept of depreciable cost in your evaluation.
questions.a: The statement is false. Total depreciation charged over the asset's life always equals the depreciable cost (cost – net residual value), regardless of useful life. Extending life reduces the annual charge but does not change the total. A student who agrees confuses annual depreciation with total depreciation, indicating a lack of understanding that depreciable cost is a fixed cap.

questions.q: Create a realistic scenario for a bakery purchasing an oven where the estimated useful life is expressed in "number of baking cycles" rather than years. Define all three factors and write the formula for depreciation per cycle.
questions.a: Scenario: Oven cost ₹4,00,000 + ₹20,000 installation = ₹4,20,000. Estimated 1,00,000 baking cycles over its life. Net residual value ₹50,000. Depreciable cost = ₹3,70,000. Depreciation per cycle = ₹3,70,000 / 1,00,000 = ₹3.70 per cycle. A poor answer uses years instead of cycles or omits installation cost, showing the student cannot adapt the useful-life concept to non-time units as permitted by AS-6.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The amount of ______ charged each accounting period is determined by three factors: the original cost of the asset (including all expenditures to make it ready for use), the estimated net residual value (scrap value after disposal costs), and the estimated useful life (the period over which the asset is expected to generate economic benefits for the enterprise).

Fill in the blank: Imagine your family buys a delivery van for ₹8,00,000, spends ₹50,000 on ______ and fitting shelves, and expects to sell it after 5 years for ₹1,20,000 (but will pay ₹20,000 towing and advertising to sell it).
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can independently compute the depreciable cost and annual depreciation charge (straight-line method) for a given asset when provided with purchase price, incidental costs, estimated scrap value, disposal expenses, and useful life, and can explain how a change in any one factor alters the depreciation amount.
